paragraphs: Friend, here's what sits heavy on me about this one. Israel had the right outrage. Gibeah's men did a terrible thing, and Israel asked for justice: "Hand over the wicked men of Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge Israel of this evil." (Judges 20:13) But Benjamin would not hand them over, and the whole tribe took the side of the wrong. When we protect our own people instead of the truth, everybody ends up paying for it.

Now look at how Israel kept going back to God. After 22,000 fell, they wept before the LORD (Judges 20:23). After 18,000 more, they sat weeping, fasted and presented offerings (Judges 20:26). They even asked, "should we stop?" and the LORD answered, "Fight, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand." (Judges 20:28) I think the lesson is that big numbers don't win anything, and the text says it plainly: "The LORD defeated Benjamin in the presence of Israel." (Judges 20:35) 400,000 swordsmen, and the win still wasn't theirs to take credit for.

So what do you do with that, baker? When you're sure you're right, and even when you're sure you're strong, you still go ask God before you move. Don't lean on your own numbers, your own plan or your own confidence. And hold on to this: the story isn't over, and the weight of this chapter is a reason to keep listening for what comes next.
